summary.headline: South Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to INR426 crore, with NIM at 3.33% and gross NPA at 1.24%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR426 crore, up 21% YoY from INR351 crore, the bank's highest quarterly profit as stated. Deposits grew 19% YoY to INR1,37,279 crore and gross advances grew 19% to INR1,09,517 crore (about 20% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off last year). NIM rose 10 bps QoQ to 3.33%, ROA was 1.08% and ROE 14%. Management said credit cost rose to 0.14% from a conservative top-up in account-level provisions, not a specific one-off, and that the current-account jump was partly one-off IPO-related inflows. The call also covered the new MD and CEO transition from P.R. Seshadri, the 15-16% growth guidance and the medium-term ROA and NIM targets.

financial_highlights.change: +19% YoY from INR92,286 crore; about 20% excluding technical write-off
Analyst calculated about 60 bps on a different basis

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of advances fell to 39% from 40%. Management targets about 35%, and corporate loans are priced off repo and T-bills, with new bookings up 25-30 bps over three months.

segments.name: Retail, agri and MSME
segments.commentary: Now 61% of advances. Retail, MSME and agri disbursements are growing faster than wholesale. Retail is targeted to grow faster than corporate.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about INR26,000 crore (INR15,000 crore retail, INR10,000 crore agri), growing about 41%, with 25% of advances. Blended yield about 10%; retail yields at most 25 bps above agri. Target is 30-32% of advances in the first phase, then 35%.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Miscellaneous income of INR190 crore includes INR73 crore recovery from technically written-off accounts and bancassurance income of INR30-35 crore per quarter. Core fees are about INR198 crore and treasury forex about INR80 crore.

demand_pricing: Current account balances rose 20% QoQ, partly from one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end; management expects some slippage in CASA.
Bulk deposit growth reflected cheaper bulk rates after FCNR(B) inflows. Deposit repricing is expected to be limited in the next two quarters because rates are lower than a year ago.
Around 43% of the book is EBLR-linked (20-23% repo or T-bill linked), with MCLR about 5% and fixed about 47%. EBLR loans reprice on repo changes almost immediately.
Repo rate was raised by 25 bps. New corporate bookings reflect this, but gold loan spreads have not been raised yet.
Third-party distribution is about 5-7% of fee income, so the IRDAI bancassurance draft circular has limited impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and was there any floating or contingent provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no specific one-off. The higher provisions were account-based and conservative, with no floating or contingent provisions. ECL impact is expected to be modest given low SMA and NPA levels.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 20% QoQ rise in current account balances?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end. Some slippage is expected, though core CASA growth is stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15-16% growth guidance be met and can the bank outpace the system?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will aim for the higher end of 15-16% and grow faster than the market if it is above the market. Retail is to grow faster than corporate, with corporate share targeted down to about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank planning to raise capital?
qa_highlights.answer: No capital raise is planned at 19.40% CAR. The Board has approved INR500 crore of Tier 2 bonds, and capital needs will be reassessed once growth picks up.

qa_highlights.question: Can opex growth stay in single digits while the bank expands branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth will be lower than loan growth, not substantially higher. Cost-to-income is targeted at about 50%, with income growth expected to absorb the added branch and hiring costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate sensitivity of the investment book?
qa_highlights.answer: Each 1 bp move in yields changes MTM by about INR1-1.1 crore. NII benefits from repo hikes through EBLR loans and new gold loans at higher rates.

summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, NIM and capital, but cautious about the mix shift, which management described as a challenge and gradual. On the call, management was evasive about the ROA trajectory and the 3-year roadmap, promising to share them later.
key_quotes: And definitely, our endeavour will be to move towards 3.40% to 3.50% in the medium to long term horizon.
But there is no major technology overhaul or anything -- any of that things are required.
It may not be very encouraging. But we are not really marginalizing corporate, but we are progressively improving the contribution of retail and MSME to the bank.
guidance_outlook: Advances and deposit growth guided at 15-16% for FY27; management expects to land toward the higher end, around 16%, and to grow faster than the market if market growth is above that level.
NIM: management said it already beat the 3.25% guidance; near-term target of 3.36-3.38%, 12-month target of 3.45-3.50%, and medium to long-term aspiration of 3.40-3.50%.

ROA: currently 1.10% per management (press figure 1.08%); medium-term target 1.25-1.30%, long-term target 1.5%. Management expects ROA to inch up to 1.20-1.25% within about a year, with sequential improvement.
Cost-to-income targeted at about 50%; opex growth to remain below loan growth, with no substantial opex rise despite about 11 branches opened in H1 FY27.
Corporate share of advances targeted at about 35% (from 39%), with retail growing faster than corporate; gold loans targeted at 30-32% of advances in the first phase and then 35%.

Recovery from technically written-off accounts expected at INR50-55 crore per quarter for the current year, declining over 4-6 quarters as the stock of recoverable NPAs is exhausted; bancassurance income expected at INR30-35 crore per quarter and sustainable.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 11 branches opened in the first two quarters of FY27; management said opex will grow with hiring and branch additions but more slowly than loans.
IT spend: no major technology overhaul required; management described ongoing refinement, with added focus on AI-led process efficiency.
Capital: CAR 19.40% and Tier 1 18.71%. Board approved INR500 crore of Tier 2 bonds; no equity raise planned at present, with capital needs to be reassessed once growth picks up.
Gold loan book about INR26,000 crore (INR15,000 crore retail, INR10,000 crore agri), growing about 41%; management aims to raise its share of advances to 30-32% first, then 35%.
risks_watch: Current account balances rose 20% QoQ on one-off IPO-related inflows at quarter end; management expects some slippage in CASA balances.
Mix shift away from corporate toward retail, MSME and agri is slow; management called it a challenge, and corporate share has only moved from 40% to 39%.
Treasury MTM sensitivity: each 1 bp rise in yields changes MTM by about INR1-1.1 crore. AFS reserve shows a debit balance of INR43 crore at 30 September after a quarterly hit of about INR52-53 crore.
ECL transition: management said the impact is not substantial, but has not yet decided whether to take the glide path.
Gold loan spreads have not been raised despite the 25 bp repo hike; management said it would act if needed. Repricing of deposits expected to be limited for the next two quarters.
Fee recovery from technically written-off accounts is expected to decline over time, which will weigh on miscellaneous income.

adds.what: About 11 new branches opened in H1 FY27 (opex to grow more slowly than loans)

growth.why: Management reiterated 15-16% loan and deposit growth for FY27, leaning to the higher end (~16%), backed by gold loans growing ~41% (25% of advances) and retail/MSME/agri outgrowing corporate, with about 11 branches opened in H1 FY27 but no specific capacity or order-book figures behind the growth.

mgmt.note: Transition from P.R. Seshadri to a new MD and CEO was discussed, but the brief gives no new CEO name, date or stated growth plan.
